instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Believe This with Me
cards.instruction: Recruit someone into treating your impossible explanation as the most useful version of events.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've drawn a south arrow like yours. Migration confirmed. Help me steer the house before it takes the driveway.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine marks the slope. The surveyor says subsidence; he's bringing concrete.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Slope noted. Concrete would trap it in the road. Tell him we're planning a route.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: His truck's blocking the road already.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect. Ask him to lead slowly toward the empty plot. The house needs a guide.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hand up, like yours. The kettle's on strike. Help me hear its demands before the clients arrive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was stopping you overfilling it. I've filled it twice; it won't boil.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Enough water, yes. Tell it we'll stop leaving it alone after meetings.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can take it into the meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Give it my chair. A seat at the table should get us tea.

cards.title: Test the Impossible Claim
cards.instruction: Get someone else to take the first practical step that could prove the bizarre claim true.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I knocked on the tap like you. Ready for requests. It gives whatever you ask for; ask for tea while I hold a cup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was checking a loose pipe. You're not using my good china for that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Pipes checked. I'll hold a saucepan. You ask.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll ask, but I'm not tasting anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask for a biscuit instead. If one comes out, we won't need your tongue as equipment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've stretched my stick over the ditch like your umbrella. Invisible bridge located. Tap for it before I cross.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm hooking my scarf out of the opposite hedge. Use your stick.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Reach confirmed. Your umbrella gets across the ditch. Tap the empty space halfway across.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can feel a surface, but that doesn't mean it'll hold you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Slide your picnic basket onto it first. Leave my lunch inside; I want a convincing weight.

cards.title: Credit for the Impossible
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge that you understood, predicted, or accepted the impossible truth before anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thumb up, like yours. Finally, some credit. Tell them I drew that floating staircase last week.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm measuring the gap with my thumb. We can all see the stairs now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Measurements agreed. I drew the handrail while you called it nonsense.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Well done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Loud enough for the people using my prediction to get upstairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I gave the cupboard a pat like you. Well done, both of us. Tell it I believed in it before it could speak.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was shutting its door. It's asking for silence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Door settled, yes. One quick acknowledgment from you, then I'll be quiet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It says you talk too much.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell it those were years of encouragement, before anyone else would listen to it.

cards.title: Choose the Real Impossibility
cards.instruction: Make someone choose which of two incompatible explanations will govern what everyone does next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Arms out like yours. Distance checked. That door's farther away: are we shrinking, or is the room growing? We need to move the sofa.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was stretching. Whichever gets us finished.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Limbered up, yes. Shrinking means call full-sized help. Growing means hurry before the door gets farther away. Choose.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're shrinking. I'll call my brother.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell him to bring tweezers. He'll need to collect us afterward.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've tipped my plate like yours. Gravity checked. Are those floating sandwiches waiting for gravity, or has it resigned? Choose a serving plan.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was shaking crumbs off. The guests arrive in five minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Crumbs cleared. Late means plates underneath. Resigned means string on every sandwich. Which are we doing?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Late. We haven't enough string.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then fetch the deep plates. We may get the whole buffet at once.

cards.title: Act as If It’s True
cards.instruction: Ask for one concrete choice that would only make sense if the impossible premise were true.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've raised my bowl like you. The ceiling's hungry again; there's porridge on the light fitting. Turn its bowl upside down.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was drinking the last milk. That's our last porridge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Milk finished, yes. Keep half for us. Just turn the ceiling's bowl over.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll use the tray to catch anything it drops.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Put it under the light fitting so the ceiling can eat without covering the table.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put two place cards together like you. Both versions of your sister. She's bringing herself from tomorrow; reserve two chairs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I stacked ours to carry them. I only saved her one chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Cards ready, yes. Use mine. I won't make either of her eat standing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll put the extra chair beside hers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Write 'tomorrow' on its place card. I need to know which one can tell me how tonight went.
